bear.narrative: A genuine down cycle, not a slower recovery. The replacement calender slips again, so its first full year moves from FY2027E to FY2028E, and the import flood does not ease: revenue grows 5.6pp a year less than the base - the mirror image of the bull - which leaves FY2029E growth barely above inflation and FY2030E below it. Dumped plastic keeps domestic utilisation near the 60-70% the association reports, the trade remedies INAPLAS asked for at the November 2026 meeting with the industry ministry are not imposed, resin costs stay near the deck's FY2026E Brent of 96.0 and the 15% unpassed exposure bites harder, taking the at-cost gross margin down 5.5pp so the reported FY2026E margin falls below the FY2025 11.8% trough. Working capital absorbs more cash. The controller loan is called and refinanced on the bank lines, whose cost is the interest differential only - about IDR3.1bn a year pre-tax, roughly IDR1.7 a share a year - so the bear does not carry a higher discount rate: a call is cash-neutral and raising the cost of capital for it would double-count the loan already in the bridge [S2, S4, S5, F12, F21]. The free-float placement is not a bear shock: a placement at the market price is value-neutral per share and a discounted one costs about 1.5% of intrinsic value, disclosed in section 5 rather than modelled as a down-cycle event [S0, S2].

bull.narrative: The calender alone, running from the first quarter of 2027 at close to nameplate, is the bull: the machine is paid for and its capacity is already installed, so revenue grows 5.6pp a year faster than the base and reaches about 82% of the 29,600 MT productive base by FY2030E, which is 69% of the 35,000 MT nameplate. The fixed factory overhead of IDR59.8bn spreads across those tonnes, lifting the at-cost gross margin 5.5pp; the reported margin reaches, but does not exceed, the FY2023 peak of 24.9% by FY2030E. Working capital turns quicker as volume fills the plant and the PP and HIPS line finally earns its capital [S2, F11, F26, F5]. We deliberately do not put the import remedy or a lower cost of capital in the bull: a remedy is a separate policy event worth more than this and is treated as a sensitivity in section 5, and a lower discount rate would be a second view of the same risk rather than a mirrored shock [S4, S5].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +11.5% to IDR335.0bn, which requires nothing but the run-rate already delivered. Nine-month 2026 revenue was IDR247.30bn and the September quarter alone was the difference between the nine-month and the six-month figures, IDR87.58bn, so a fourth quarter that simply holds the third quarter delivers IDR334.88bn [S7, F30, F43]. The prior version's IDR347.9bn needed a fourth quarter 15% above the third, and no filing after 30 September 2026 supports a commissioning: the September accounts carry total assets under construction of IDR36.80bn with no reclassification out of it, machine additions in the quarter of only IDR4.04bn, and the company's last statement is that the machine would run after mid-2026 [S7, S2, F23, F40]. We therefore put no calender contribution in FY2026E and let the machine's first quarter of output land in FY2027E; a further slip moves that to FY2028E but does not remove the capacity. Even so FY2026E is 36% below the company's own IDR520.94bn target, a target it missed by 21% in 2025 [S2, F17, F19]. FY2027E +15.5% to IDR387.0bn is the first full year of the replacement calender and is still below the FY2024 peak of IDR399.7bn [S0]. FY2028E +11.0%, FY2029E +8.5% and FY2030E +7.0% fill capacity that is already installed rather than new capital, and taper toward the 3.0% long run, which is the house terminal-growth cap rather than a deck series. Implied utilisation, at the FY2025 revenue per tonne of IDR27.39m and on the 29,600 MT productive base, is 41.3% in FY2026E, 47.7% in FY2027E, 53.0% in FY2028E, 57.5% in FY2029E and 61.5% in FY2030E, on the single stated divisor of IDR27.39m of FY2025 revenue per tonne applied to the 29,600 MT productive base (IDR810.7bn of full-base revenue); on the full 35,000 MT nameplate those are 34.9%, 40.4%, 44.8%, 48.6% and 52.0% [S2, F5, F6, F26]. The FY2030E figure is inside the 60-70% band the industry association reports for domestic plants today, which is the test the previous version of this model failed [S4, S5].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: 20.2% at FY2025A input costs, flat. This is a margin-at-normal-utilisation judgement, not a forecast of the reported margin, and the bridge from the last undisrupted year is explicit. FY2024 earned 17.2% at roughly 14,600 MT, about 49% of the 29,600 MT productive base [S2, S0]. Factory overhead was IDR59.76bn in FY2025, or IDR5.45m per tonne at 10,970 MT and about IDR4.09m per tonne at FY2024 volume; at the 18,900 MT implied by FY2030E revenue it falls to about IDR3.16m per tonne, which on revenue per tonne of IDR27.39m is worth about 3.4pp of gross margin [S2, F5, F11]. Adding that absorption to FY2024's 17.2% gives about 20.6%; we hold 20.2% to allow for the PP and HIPS line, which the company concedes has not delivered the returns expected of it, and for a mix that is less favourable than FY2024's [S2, F26]. The ten-year reported range in the annual report's financial highlights is 17.6, 14.4, 13.4, 17.7, 14.5, 15.0, 20.7, 24.9, 17.2 and 11.8 per cent, so 20.2% at normal volume sits between the average and the FY2023 peak rather than at the peak [S2]. The FY2026E-FY2030E reported margin is then 16.8%, 18.2%, 18.7%, 19.0% and 19.4% once the Brent link is applied, because the deck's Brent is 41% above the FY2025 average in FY2026E and only 10% above it by FY2030E [S0]. The nine-month 2026 actual margin of 16.55% and the third-quarter 17.3% are the anchor for the FY2026E figure [S7]. We deliberately do not carry the 24.9% of FY2023: that year had a 41% lower resin cost and no import flood, and the associations now put industry utilisation at 60-70% because of dumped imports [S4, S5].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: 0.70, the raw-material share of cost of goods sold: IDR186.03bn of raw materials against IDR264.89bn of COGS in FY2025, with factory overhead at IDR59.76bn (22.6%), direct labour at IDR19.09bn and packing at IDR3.52bn [S2, F10, F11]. The resins are petrochemical - polypropylene, polyethylene and PET sheet - so Brent prices the feedstock; the company itself attributes the FY2025 margin compression partly to raw-material and energy prices [S2]. We do not use 1.0 because roughly 30% of COGS is rupiah overhead, wages and packaging that do not move with oil.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: 0.85, and this is an explicit judgment, not a sourced fact. The annual report contains no pricing-policy statement: searches for harga jual, menyesuaikan harga and kenaikan harga return no passage in which the company says it sets prices to cover costs, so the previous version's citation of S2 for that proposition was wrong and is withdrawn. The number is a judgment about a made-to-order industrial converter with no customer above 10% of revenue, which gives it more room to reprice than a branded consumer business but less than a producer with a tight market [S2, F25]. It is not 1.0 because the industry association says domestic plants run at only 60-70% of capacity because imported plastic is being sold at dumping prices, which caps how much of a cost rise can be pushed into price [S4, S5]. The value sensitivity is direct: at 100% pass-through the FY2026E reported gross margin is about 3.4pp higher than at 85%, taking it to the 20.2% at-cost level, and at 70% it is about 3.4pp lower, about 13.3%, because the retained exposure is 0.70 x (1 - pass-through) of COGS applied to a Brent move of 41% [S0]. The 70% case does not return to the FY2025 trough of 11.8% because volumes have recovered by then; it is the margin the plant earns if it recovers none of the resin increase. We use 85% because the nine-month 2026 gross margin of 16.55% was earned with Brent averaging well above the FY2025 level, which is evidence that most of the cost move was recovered in price [S7].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 12.8% on the model's IDR335.0bn of revenue, i.e. about IDR42.9bn of selling and general-and-administrative cost, up from IDR41.84bn in FY2025 because selling cost scales with the recovered volume [S2]. Nine-month 2026 selling and administrative cost was IDR32.65bn on revenue of IDR247.30bn, 13.2%, so IDR42.9bn for the year requires the fourth quarter to run at about 11.7% - IDR10.2bn on the fourth quarter's IDR87.7bn - which is what the shrinking electronics business supports [S7, S2, F9]. The ratio then falls to 11.9%, 11.2%, 10.8% and 10.5% as revenue grows against a largely fixed cost base: the FY2025 ratio was 13.9% only because revenue collapsed 24.8% under a fixed establishment, and the FY2023 ratio on IDR469.1bn of sales was 10.7% [S2, F20]. The electronics business, which lost IDR2.29bn at the operating line in FY2025 on IDR7.43bn of sales, is being scaled down and its cost is the first to go [S2, F9]. We stop at 10.5% rather than the FY2023 10.7% because the new calender adds depreciation and technical staff rather than removing them.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A was IDR29.16bn against revenue of IDR300.47bn, 9.7%, once the fixed-asset note is used instead of the data pack's selling-and-G&A share of 5.98 [S2, F1, F2]. The ratio falls to 9.2% in FY2026E and 7.7% by FY2030E because the denominator grows while the charge grows only with the IDR40bn of 2026 capital spending; the absolute charge rises from IDR32.0bn to IDR40.0bn.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 14.6% of the model's IDR335.0bn of revenue, or IDR48.9bn, which is 14.9% above the IDR42.553bn of additions booked in the nine months to 30 September 2026 [S7, F39]; the difference is a fourth quarter of about IDR6.4bn for completion of the machine plus routine maintenance, rebased on the nine-month filing. Of the nine-month additions, IDR36.798bn is the total assets-under-construction balance at that date; the filing does not break AUC by project and never names the calender, so we treat the balance as the machine without asserting the split, and the project's cost is between IDR36.8bn capitalised and IDR49.2bn once the IDR12.352bn of machinery advances is added [S7, F40, F42]; cash advances for fixed assets were IDR46.655bn and the advance balance rose from IDR8.250bn to IDR12.352bn, so the nine-month cash outlay sits IDR4.10bn above the additions booked [S7, F41, F42]. FY2025 capex was IDR36.52bn against D&A of IDR29.16bn [S2, F1, S0]. From FY2027E we hold capex at 7.7% falling to 6.4%, roughly equal to D&A, because the machine is installed and what remains is maintenance plus the PP sheet line, which the annual report says did not deliver the returns expected of it [S2]. We do not carry a second expansion: the productive base is 29,600 MT against 10,970 MT produced, so the next rupiah of growth comes from filling the plant, not building another.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 21% in FY2026E, 19% thereafter. The FY2025 ratio was 20.8% on the data pack's working-capital line against revenue, but the June 2026 balance sheet shows inventory and receivables rebuilt ahead of the machine restart, which is why we start above the FY2024 ratio of 16.7% and let it normalise as the stock converts to sales [S0, S2]. The FY2025 inventory build and the IDR2.36bn rise in taxes payable are in the same filing [S2].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22%, the Indonesian corporate rate. The FY2025 effective rate was 19.4% (tax IDR1.35bn on pre-tax profit IDR6.98bn) and FY2024 was 25.5%, so the statutory rate is the neutral assumption rather than either year's accident [S2]. The nine-month 2026 effective rate was 37.0% (tax IDR4.39bn on pre-tax profit IDR11.84bn), which the tax note explains rather than leaving as an assumption: note 18d reconciles the parent's pre-tax profit of IDR12.753bn to taxable income of IDR19.932bn through IDR8.550bn of temporary differences, of which IDR6.669bn is book-over-tax depreciation and IDR1.881bn employee-benefit provisions, less IDR1.371bn of final-taxed interest income, and note 18e applies the 22% statutory rate to that taxable income [S7]. The gap is the depreciation timing difference, which reverses as the new machine is depreciated for tax, not a higher statutory rate, so 22% on book profit is the right forward rate once the difference normalises; if the depreciation gap persisted the effective rate would stay near the nine-month figure and FY2026E net profit would be roughly a fifth lower, which section 3 discloses [S7, S2].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 7.44%, FY2025 finance costs of IDR1.668bn over opening debt of IDR22.424bn of short-term bank loans [S2, F3]. This rate is used for interest expense on the bank lines in the profit and loss, NOT for the WACC: the engine builds the pre-tax cost of debt in the cost of capital as the rupiah risk-free rate plus the deck's corporate debt spread, which is 9.45%, and the 7.44% input does not enter that calculation. The distinction is stated in the report so the prose matches the model. The rate is applied to bank borrowings only: the IDR41.15bn controller loan that sits in the same note is non-interest-bearing, so including it in the base would understate the true cost of the bank lines [S2, F12, F13].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 1.70%, the FY2025 yield rebased on the cash base that actually existed during 2026. The engine applies the yield to opening cash of IDR115.97bn, but IDR60bn of that was paid out on 26 June 2026 and the nine-month accounts show finance income of IDR1.438bn, an annualised IDR1.92bn, or 1.65% of the opening balance [S0, S7, S3, F21]. Using 1.70% reconciles the FY2026E finance line to the filing instead of applying the pre-dividend yield to a balance that no longer existed for the whole year; the previous 2.87% overstated FY2026E net profit by about IDR1.3bn [S7].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company repaid IDR1.39bn of short-term bank loans in FY2025 and has net cash; the dividend is funded from the balance sheet, not from new debt [S2, S3]. The 30 September 2026 balance sheet confirms it: bank loans fell a further IDR0.87bn to IDR26.03bn while cash rose to IDR41.23bn [S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero from FY2026E. FY2025 carried IDR11.91bn of other income of which IDR8.74bn was the fire insurance claim and IDR0.22bn a gain on asset sales, plus IDR0.61bn of other expense; none of it repeats [S2, F15, F16]. The nine-month 2026 accounts carry IDR3.93bn of other income, of which IDR0.63bn is a gain on asset sales and IDR3.30bn is an unexplained lain-lain line, and IDR0.40bn of other expense; we exclude all of it from the forecast because the nature of the lain-lain item is not disclosed and it is not an operating cash flow [S7]. Excluding the FY2025 items, the FY2025 operating result was a loss of IDR6.2bn, which is the trough the forecast recovers from.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the minority interest in the consolidated subsidiary is immaterial in both FY2025 and FY2024 [S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 25% from FY2026E, which is deliberately NOT the FY2025 payout. The Rp44.03 a share approved on 25 May 2026 covers FY2025 and the previous financial year in one payment, cost about IDR60bn and was 10.7 times FY2025 net profit; it is a catch-up distribution out of retained earnings, not a policy rate, and it is already paid (26 June 2026) before the valuation balance sheet [S3, F21]. The engine pays last year's declared DPS, so the FY2026E cash flow carries the IDR60bn correctly. After it, cash fell from IDR116.0bn at end-2025 to IDR31.2bn at 30 June 2026 and has since rebuilt to IDR41.2bn at 30 September 2026, and the group is in net debt once the controller loan is counted, so the next dividend has to be funded from earnings [S0, S2, S7, F12]. The dividend policy in the annual report is discretionary, decided at each AGM, with no ratio [S2]; the record is a skipped dividend for FY2022, IDR7.49bn for FY2023 and this catch-up, so we assume a modest 25% rather than a return to the Rp44.03 level.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero in the forecast, with the free-float placement quantified rather than modelled. 1,362,671,400 shares are issued and paid up and no rights issue is announced [S2, S0]. The data pack's free float is 7.81% against the exchange's 15% minimum for holders below 5%, a gap of 7.19pp on the registry measure; the annual report states the 15% rule but gives no phase-in date we can source, so we treat the deadline as unspecified [S0, S2]; closing it by placing new shares at the current price would need about 115.3m new shares, an 8.5% increase, raising about IDR29.75bn at IDR258 [S0, S2]. That is close to value-neutral per share: the cash raised at the market price is worth approximately what the new shares dilute, so a placement at the current price does not reduce the DCF value per share and is not put through the share count, which the engine applies to the profit-and-loss lines but not to the DCF denominator. A discounted placement is a real cost and is carried in the bear narrative, where a 20% discount would cost about 1.5% of intrinsic value per share. The annual report itself links the free-float rule to the buyback: it says a buyback is constrained by the rule that at least 15% must be held by the public below 5%, which is why the unused buyback authorization was not used [S2].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.0%, the house terminal-growth cap for a rupiah name: a rounded midpoint of the deck's rupiah long-run inflation anchor and its CPI assumption, below the template's IDR terminal cap and below the 5.29% real GDP growth the deck carries for Indonesia, because a converter with 70% of COGS in a globally traded feedstock grows with volume and resin prices, not with nominal GDP [S0]. It is not itself a deck series, and the report describes it as a house cap rather than as the deck's inflation rate.

challenges.challenge: The note says the September quarter was flat on revenue and its gross margin was below the June quarter's, but the only cited data are cumulative: 6M revenue 159.72 and gross profit 25.78 (16.14 per cent), 9M 247.30 and 40.93 (16.55 per cent), so Q3 is derivable as 87.58 revenue and 15.15 gross profit, a 17.30 per cent margin. On the cited facts Q3 revenue is 9.7 per cent above the H1 average quarter and its margin is 1.16pp above the 6M rate. No Q1 or Q2-only filing is in fund record. The sentence is cited to F43 and F44, which do not say it.
challenges.answer: Withdrew the flat-quarter sentence. Q3 derives as 87.58bn revenue, 9.7% above the H1 average quarter, and 17.30% gross margin against 16.14% for 6M; report now says the quarter added more than the H1 average with a higher margin, and summary and thesis are rebuilt on that.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of 347.95 requires Q4 revenue of 100.65bn, 15 per cent above Q3's 87.58 and 25 per cent above Q4 2025's 80.25. The only machine evidence is the FY2025 annual report estimate that it would run after mid-2026 and the 30 Sep 2026 filing showing AUC of 36.80bn with no reclassification out of it and mesin additions of only 4.04bn; there is no post-30-September commissioning statement. The base case therefore assumes a day-one Q4 restart of a machine the company has already delayed once.
challenges.answer: No post-30-Sep commissioning source exists, so FY2026E growth is cut to 11.5% (IDR335.0bn), which needs only a Q4 that holds the Q3 run-rate; no calender output in FY2026E, first full year FY2027E at IDR387.0bn, and the slip risk is stated as moving that to FY2028E.

challenges.challenge: The report and the drift.capex justification state that IDR36.798bn of AUC is the replacement calender. F40 is total assets under construction; the 30 Sep filing never uses the word calender and the fixed-asset note shows only a total AUC line. The IDR12.352bn of advances is described as advances for machineries and equipment and could be the unpaid balance of the same machine, so the total project cost is not established.
challenges.answer: IDR36.798bn is now described as the total assets-under-construction balance, not the calender; the filing never names it, so project cost is given as the range between the capitalised balance and that balance plus IDR12.352bn of machinery advances.

challenges.challenge: The bear adds 1pp to the WACC for a controller-loan call while the base already deducts the same loan at face. A call is cash-neutral (cash less 41.15, bank debt plus 41.15); its real cost is the interest differential, about IDR3.1bn a year pre-tax, or roughly Rp1.7 a share a year, not 1pp of WACC on a DCF that is 49 per cent terminal value (worth about minus 20 per cent). Charging both is a double count and it widens the scenario spread.
challenges.answer: The 1pp WACC shock is removed from the bear. A call is cash-neutral and costs only the IDR3.1bn interest differential, roughly IDR1.7 a share a year, which the bear narrative now states instead of a discount-rate change.

challenges.challenge: The IDR41.15bn controller loan is deducted at face because the note treats it as callable, but the only sourcing is the absence of a term (F13). The balance is unchanged at 41.15 across 30 Sep 2026, 31 Dec 2025 and FY2024, carries no covenant and there is no evidence of a call. At face the deduction costs about Rp15.4 a share against the half-face reading the note itself computes, roughly 6 per cent of the DCF and about 12 rupiah on the target.
challenges.answer: The loan is now carried at present value, about IDR20.5bn against IDR41.15bn face, because no filing evidences a call and the balance is unchanged across three balance-sheet dates; the call is a bear event valued at the interest differential.

challenges.challenge: 9M2026 operating cash flow was IDR25.61bn against IDR7.46bn of net profit and IDR7.76bn in the same period of 2025, on capex of IDR46.66bn, so the machine is being funded from operations and cash still rose to IDR41.23bn after a IDR60bn dividend. The report contains no cash-flow, accruals or free-cash-flow cover analysis at all, and the strongest evidence that the recovery is real is left out of both the base and the bull.
challenges.answer: Added the cash-conversion evidence to section 3: nine-month operating cash flow well above net profit, capex of IDR42.6bn covered from operations, cash at IDR41.2bn after the June dividend, and cited it as the reason the bull is a genuine path.

challenges.challenge: The bull requires three simultaneous events: the calender at nameplate, an import remedy, and a 1pp lower WACC. The method card requires scenarios to shock the same drivers in a mirrored way and the base rate to anchor the probability. As built, the 25 per cent bull is a joint tail at Rp727 rather than the most likely upside path, and the report concedes that if a remedy is imposed the bull weight is too low.
challenges.answer: Bull rebuilt on the calender alone: the import remedy and the lower WACC are removed, so the bull mirrors the bear on the same three operating drivers; the remedy is now a separate sensitivity stated in section 5.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says the free-float gap is closed by a discounted placement, but share_change is zero in all three scenarios and the placement never enters the model. The assumption text quantifies about 1.5 per cent of intrinsic value for a 20 per cent discount and then drops it. At 7.81 per cent free float against a 15 per cent rule, with IDR107.6m a day of turnover, the placement is the most concrete dilutive event in the file.
challenges.answer: The discounted placement is removed from the bear narrative and the share count stays unchanged; section 5 now states that a deep-discount placement costs a couple of per cent of intrinsic value and that this is where the dilution is valued.

challenges.challenge: The 31 March 2029 free-float deadline appears in fund record, report section 5 and the catalyst list, sourced to S0 and S2. S2 states only that the exchange rule requires at least 15 per cent held by the public below 5 per cent; it gives no date, and S0 is a Yahoo data pack. The 30 June 2027 trade-remedy date is likewise cited to S5, a November 2026 news article that sets no timetable.
challenges.answer: Deleted the 31 March 2029 deadline and the 30 June 2027 remedy date from the catalyst list and prose; both are now described as having no phase-in date or timetable we can source.

challenges.challenge: The rating is manufactured by the 20 per cent illiquidity discount applied after the probability weighting: the pre-discount tree is Rp323, about 25 per cent upside and ADD territory, and 0.8 times 323 is Rp258, a 0.9 per cent return. At a 10 per cent discount the target is Rp291, about 13 per cent upside, an ADD; doubling the bear weight to 50 per cent gives Rp271 pre-discount and Rp217 after, a SELL. The conclusion turns entirely on one discretionary input that the commodity-cyclical contract does not contain.
challenges.answer: The 20% is not discretionary: it is the house liquidity schedule for names below IDR500m ADTV, and the report now says so, discloses that the rating is band-driven, and states that a doubling of turnover into the next band would make the target an ADD and a fall below the lowest band a SELL. The honest base takes the target to IDR246.

challenges.challenge: The model uses a 22 per cent tax rate against a 9M2026 effective rate of 37.0 per cent (tax 4.385 on PBT 11.844), justified only as a timing item with no citation to the tax note. Cash tax paid in the period was only 0.79bn, so much of the charge is likely deferred, but the report does not show that. If 37 per cent is the run rate, FY2026E net profit falls from 12.14 to about 9.8 and the DPS and ROE cross-checks fall with it.
challenges.answer: Cited the reconciliation: note 18d bridges parent PBT of IDR12.753bn to taxable income of IDR19.932bn through IDR8.550bn of temporary differences, of which IDR6.669bn is book-over-tax depreciation, and note 18e applies 22%; the 37% is a timing difference, not a run rate, and the sensitivity is disclosed.

challenges.challenge: The summary calls the clean operating margin middle single digits. Clean operating profit is 8.29bn on 247.30bn of revenue, 3.3 per cent, because 3.93bn of the 11.81bn reported operating profit is other income and 0.40bn is other expense. Middle single digits describes the reported figure, not the clean one.
challenges.answer: The report now distinguishes the reported operating margin, part of which is other income, from the clean margin after stripping other income and expense, which is low single digits.

challenges.challenge: The commodity-cyclical output contract asks for NAV at spot alongside NAV at through-cycle price, and for the realisation basis. The report declines the spot NAV with a reason that is defensible, but it does not give the through-cycle NAV in a comparable form or any seasonality or realisation statement, so a reader cannot see how much of the target is cycle position.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now gives the realisation basis and states why a spot-flat NAV is not published: spot is above the long-run price only in FY2027E to FY2029E and the move is bounded inside one cell of the operating grid.

challenges.challenge: Several fact tags do not support the sentence they are attached to: 147 employees and the site description cite F6, which is installed capacity; the electronics re-scoping cites F9, which is the revenue split; the 42 per cent capex-turnaround base rate cites S0, not data/base_rates.yaml. The summary also types IDR-6.2bn, IDR8.7bn, IDR11.9bn and IDR5.6bn as numerals in prose rather than through tokens.
challenges.answer: Re-pointed the fact tags: employees and the site cite the data pack, the electronics re-scoping cites the annual report, and the 42% capex-turnaround base rate cites data/base_rates.yaml; typed numerals in that paragraph are replaced by model placeholders.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E PBT of 15.57 against EBIT of 13.80 implies net finance income of plus 1.77bn, but the 9M accounts show finance income of 1.438bn against finance costs of 1.409bn, a net plus 0.03bn, after the IDR60bn June dividend cut cash from 115.97 to 41.23. The cash yield is still being applied to opening cash, so FY2026E net profit is overstated by roughly 1.3bn (about 11 per cent).
challenges.answer: Cash yield rebased from 2.87% to 1.70% so the FY2026E finance line reconciles to the nine-month IDR1.438bn on the post-dividend cash base; FY2026E net profit falls by about IDR1.3bn.

missing_bull_case.note: Cash conversion is the biggest omitted positive: 9M2026 operating cash flow was IDR25.61bn against IDR7.46bn of net profit, three and a half times, and 25.6bn against 7.76bn a year earlier [S7], yet no section mentions CFO, accruals or FCF cover. The bull is also built as a joint three-way tail, not the most likely upside.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative promises a discounted free-float placement but no scenario shock carries the dilution (share_change is zero in all three runs), and a one-quarter calender slippage is only prose, not a driver shock. The 30 Sep working-capital build (receivables 42.26 vs 34.75, inventory 63.49 vs 54.27) is not tested against the flat 21% NWC assumption.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E revenue of 347.95 requires Q4 of 100.65, fifteen per cent above Q3 and twenty-five per cent above Q4 2025, from a calender with zero reclassification out of AUC at 30 Sep; no post-September commissioning date is cited. The tax rate of 22% sits below the 9M effective 37.0%, and FY2026E net finance income of plus 1.77bn contradicts the 9M actual of plus 0.03bn.

evidence_and_citations.note: The Q3-versus-June-quarter claim, the identification of the whole AUC balance as the calender, the 31 March 2029 free-float deadline and the 30 June 2027 trade-remedy date are not supported by the cited sources; several fact tags point at the wrong fact (147 employees at F6, electronics strategy at F9).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF at 100% is the correct method for a trough converter, and the loan is deducted once so it is not double counted with net debt. But the WACC is used as the shock absorber for a financing event, and the rating is set by a post-weighting 20% illiquidity discount that the method card does not contain.

bias_and_tone.note: The words flat, plateau and no further acceleration do more work than the arithmetic allows, and the clean operating margin is called middle single digits when it is 3.3% (8.29 on 247.30) once other income is stripped. The HOLD does not survive a 10pp change in the illiquidity discount.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read consistently: Brent 68.10 FY2025A to 96.00 FY2026E to 84.00 FY2027E to 75.00 long-run, rupiah 18,350 vs 18,228 spot, CPI and risk-free used in the cost of capital. The cost link is a Brent ratio so the FX basis does not enter COGS.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative: controller loan deducted at face rather than its half-face economic value (plus 15.4 a share), 20% illiquidity discount, terminal g 3.0% below the deck CPI of 3.28%, bull weight 25% against the 42% capex-turnaround base rate, NWC 21% above FY2024. Optimistic: tax 22% against 37% actual, at-cost gross margin 20.2% above the 10-year average of 16.7%.

calibration.note: The ebitda_margin BLOCK reconciles arithmetically: gross margin plus 5.0pp, SG&A plus 1.1pp, D&A minus 0.5pp equals the 5.53pp gap, and each leg is cited to S2 or S7. The capex drift is sourced to the 9M filing. Caveat: the 19% wording compares FY2026E with booked additions, not with the IDR46.66bn cash outlay.

signoff.notes: HOLD Rp246 against Rp258 is the right call on the right method. The DCF is 100% of the target, which is what VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL prescribes for a converter at the trough of its own volume cycle; the round-1 FATAL was a target struck on trough trailing multiples and the fix (100% DCF) is the correct response. The scenarios are properly mirrored - revenue plus/minus 5.6pp, gross margin plus/minus 5.5pp, NWC plus/minus 2pp - with no discount-rate shock, which is the accepted C4 remedy, and the controller loan is carried at present value (about half face) with the call left as a bear event carried in the cash flows rather than as 1pp of WACC. The cash-conversion evidence the red team asked for (9M CFO Rp25.6bn against Rp7.5bn of net profit, capex Rp46.7bn) is in the report and supports the base. Residual, not rating-moving: QC Q8 is still open in the text. Section 4 ends "That withdrawal is the whole of the change in the target; the operating forecast is untouched" while the summary and the model attribute the move to a lower revenue path (FY2026E rebased from 347.95 to 335.03) and lower finance income, partly offset by the loan at PV. The summary is the correct account; the section 4 sentence is false and should be deleted next cycle. Desk observation: this HOLD is decided by the 20% house liquidity discount (weighted Rp308 becomes Rp246), not by the operating view - a small move in the share price or a step in ADTV would flip the rating band without any change in the thesis.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the 9M actual: FY2026E revenue of 335.03 needs only a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate (87.73 vs 87.58 delivered), gross margin 20.2% at FY2025A input costs is the FY2024 17.2% plus about 3.4pp of sourced overhead absorption, and tax 22% against the 9M 37% is resolved in the tax reconciliation as timing [S2, S7]. Scenarios are mirrored on the same three operating drivers (revenue growth +/-5.6pp, gross margin +/-5.5pp, NWC +/-2pp) with base 50%, and neither wing carries a discount-rate or remedy shock [S0]. Mild conservatism: all other income is set to zero from FY2026E although 9M2026 carries IDR3.93bn [S7, F38]; mild optimism: the controller loan is deducted at PV 20.5 rather than face 41.15, a 15 rupiah a share difference the report discloses [S2, F12]. The two roughly offset; no rating-changing bias.

findings.finding: Section 4 ends by saying that the withdrawal is the whole of the change in the target and that the operating forecast is untouched, but the summary attributes the target change to a lower revenue path and lower finance income, and FY2026E revenue was rebased from 347.95 to 335.03 in this cycle. The two statements cannot both be true.
valuation.post_bs_review states cash of IDR41.27bn at 30 September while F34 is IDR41.229bn.
The gross_margin basis gives FY2030E reported margin 19.4%, but the model gross margin is 19.17% (95.57/498.65); the other four years in the list reproduce.

The weights.changed justification says the engine capitalises LTM EBITDA of about IDR10bn and LTM net profit of about IDR15bn. The model trailing EBITDA is about IDR35bn (FY2025A 22.94 + 9M2026 34.44 - 9M2025 22.18) and trailing net profit about IDR13.6bn, so the EBITDA figure does not reproduce. Both multiple legs are struck on trailing LTM figures built from the fire year - the engine capitalises LTM EBITDA of about IDR10bn and LTM net profit of about IDR15bn - which is exactly the procyclical error the commodity-cyclical card forbids, and the engine cannot re-base them on normalised mid-cycle earnings without editing the engine. Removing their weight is therefore the only way to publish a through-cycle target. Because the engine computes only methods that carry a positive weight, no multiple table or floor value exists in this model; we do not claim one, and the cross-checks the report gives are the reverse DCF and the book-value and dividend-capacity anchors, all built from model lines [S0, S2, S4, S5, F5, F7].
